title: Which World, Which Body (compiled)

voice.text: "it's only here if you manage to be reborn in this earth world and especially here in Jambudvipa and Bharat Varsha of Jambudvipa, then it's called Karma Bhoomi. Because in the place of Karma, this is where you can act to create positive Karma."

"A couple layer of worlds and that as you progress up these worlds you get closer to Shiva and they become more Shiva-like, okay, and you start from the grossest worlds that are in the earth element, earth, water, fire and air, right, and then the worlds would be deposited in the senses, sense of action, sense of knowledge,"
"Anutt, Anutt means impelling, without being impelled by anything, for no purpose, for no reason, for no pressure by anybody or anything else. This Anuttara gives rise to all things."
"that the self or the ultimate nature of all things or the universe is Shiva himself or Shiva alone, who is in reality Chaitanya, pure consciousness."
"The term is Prakriya in Sanskrit. Modality, a kind of a whole particular way of doing things, of thinking about things."
"because he is endowed with this attribute, with his nature, he is called Vyomerupi. His nature is Vyomerupi because you remember that his form is the sky."

"everything, without exception, that is said, is taught to be this Vyomar, this emptiness, both what is supreme, at the highest levels, transcendent, and right away down to everything that is inferior to that."
"because all the world... they are perishable, and where do they perish, they come to an end within Sadashiva, and so... Sadashiva, is called Dhruva, that he is firm."

claims.text: yad idaṃ vibhavātmakaṃ bhuvanajātam uktaṃ garbhīkṛtānantavicitrabhoktṛbhogyaṃ — this world-born glory-natured, wombing endless varied enjoyer-enjoyed.
tatra yad anugataṃ mahāprakāśarūpaṃ — what pervades as great-light-formed.
tat mahāsāmānyakalpaṃ paramaśivarūpam — that is like the great common, Supreme-Śiva-formed.
Paramaśiva = what pervades the whole as great light.
yat tu katipayakatipayabhedānugataṃ rūpaṃ tat tattvam — what pervades only some differences: a category.
yathā pṛthivī nāma ... samastabrahmāṇḍānugatā — as earth, pervading all world-eggs from Kālāgni to Vīrabhadra.
Partial pervasion defines tattva; earth the example.
Five principles by power-primacy; will as even-acceptance.
